questions.question: Which declaration represents the standard document type for HTML5?
questions.explanation: In HTML5, the doctype is simplified to <!DOCTYPE html>. It ensures the browser renders the page in standards mode.

questions.question: Which HTML element is considered the root element of an HTML page?
questions.explanation: The <html> element is the root element that wraps all content on the entire page.

questions.question: What kind of information does the <head> element contain?
questions.a: The main visual content of the website
questions.b: Metadata, title, and links to scripts/styles
questions.explanation: The <head> contains machine-readable information (metadata) about the document, like its title, scripts, and style sheets.

questions.question: Which attribute is used inside the <html> tag to declare the language of the Web page?
questions.explanation: The 'lang' attribute (e.g., <html lang="en">) declares the primary language of the document for accessibility and search engines.

questions.question: Is HTML tag syntax strictly case-sensitive in HTML5?
questions.a: Yes, all tags must be lowercase
questions.b: Yes, all tags must be uppercase
questions.c: No, it is case-insensitive, but lowercase is recommended
questions.d: No, but attributes must be uppercase
questions.explanation:
HTML5 is case-insensitive (e.g.,

and

both work), but the W3C recommends lowercase for cleaner, consistent code.

questions.question: What is an 'empty' (or void) HTML element?
questions.a: An element that contains no text but has child elements
questions.b: An element without a closing tag and no content
questions.c: An element that is hidden via CSS
questions.explanation:
Empty elements, like
,
, and , have no content and do not require a closing tag.

questions.question: Which <meta> tag declaration ensures the browser uses the correct character encoding?
questions.explanation: <meta charset="UTF-8"> is the standard way to set character encoding, supporting almost all characters and symbols globally.

questions.question: According to HTML5 standards, is the <title> element strictly required within the <head>?
questions.b: Yes, it is mandatory for a valid HTML document
questions.c: Only if the page is being indexed by search engines
questions.d: Yes, but only if there is no <h1> element
questions.explanation: The HTML standard requires a <title> element inside the <head> block for the document to be valid.

questions.question: What does HTML stand for?
questions.explanation: HTML stands for HyperText Markup Language, the standard authoring language for web documents.

questions.question: What is an HTML 'element' comprised of?
questions.b: A start tag, any attributes, content, and an end tag
questions.explanation: An HTML element typically encompasses the opening tag, attributes, enclosed content, and the closing tag (except void elements).

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of an HTML void (self-closing / empty) element that does not have a closing tag?
questions.explanation: <hr> (horizontal rule) is a void element in HTML and does not enclose content or require a closing tag.

questions.question: What is the correct syntax for an HTML comment?
questions.explanation: HTML comments begin with <!-- and end with --> and are ignored by the rendering engine.

questions.question: Which HTML attribute specifies the primary natural language of the document's content?
questions.explanation: The 'lang' attribute on the <html> tag (e.g. <html lang="en">) declares the document language for search engines and screen readers.

questions.question: What character encoding standard is universally recommended for modern HTML5 documents?
questions.explanation: <meta charset="UTF-8"> covers virtually all human characters and symbols worldwide and is standard for HTML5.

questions.question: Where must the <title> tag be placed inside an HTML document?
questions.explanation: The <title> element belongs inside the <head> container, providing the page title displayed on browser tabs.

questions.question: What is the root element of an HTML document that wraps all other HTML tags (except <!DOCTYPE>)?
questions.explanation: The <html> element is the document root containing the <head> and <body> elements.

questions.question: What is the role of the <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0"> tag?
questions.b: It ensures responsive scaling and viewport width matching across mobile devices
questions.c: It enables dark mode in all browsers
questions.d: It caches the HTML page in local storage
questions.explanation: The viewport meta tag configures the mobile screen viewport width and initial zoom scale for responsive design.

questions.question: Which element inside <head> defines metadata description for search engine result snippets?
questions.explanation: <meta name="description" content="..."> provides a concise page summary read by web search engines.

questions.question: What is the Document Object Model (DOM) created by the browser when loading an HTML document?
questions.a: A plain text copy of the source code
questions.b: A hierarchical, tree-structured representation of all elements and nodes that can be manipulated via JavaScript
questions.c: A binary database compiled by the web server
questions.d: An image screenshot of the initial render
questions.explanation: The DOM represents the document as a logical node tree, enabling dynamic scripting and styling via JavaScript.

questions.question: Which tag is used to specify the base URL and default target for all relative URLs in a document?
questions.explanation: The <base> tag in <head> specifies the base URI used to resolve relative links throughout the document.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the <link rel="icon" href="favicon.ico"> tag?
questions.a: It embeds a vector graphic in the header
questions.b: It designates the favicon displayed in browser tabs and bookmarks
questions.c: It loads an icon font library
questions.explanation: <link rel="icon"> defines the browser shortcut icon (favicon) associated with the page.

questions.question:
What happens if you accidentally leave out a closing tag on a non-void element like

in HTML5?
questions.a: The browser will throw a fatal JavaScript exception and stop rendering
questions.b: The browser's HTML parser applies error-recovery rules to automatically close or infer the tag
questions.c: The entire screen becomes completely blank
questions.d: The browser downloads the missing tag from W3C servers
questions.explanation: HTML5 specifications define detailed browser error recovery and tag-omission rules to parse imperfect markup gracefully.

questions.question: Are HTML tag names case-sensitive in standard HTML5?
questions.a: Yes, <DIV> and <div> are completely different elements
questions.b: No, HTML5 is case-insensitive for element names, though lowercase is standard convention
questions.d: Only when running on Linux servers
questions.explanation: HTML tag names are case-insensitive in HTML5, though lowercase is strongly recommended for readability and consistency.

questions.question: What is Quirks Mode in browser rendering engines?
questions.b: A legacy backward-compatibility mode triggered by missing or invalid <!DOCTYPE> declarations
questions.d: A browser mode that disables JavaScript
questions.explanation: If <!DOCTYPE html> is missing, browsers enter Quirks Mode, emulating legacy 1990s layout bugs for backward compatibility.

questions.question: Which of the following is a boolean attribute in HTML (where presence alone implies true)?
questions.explanation: Boolean attributes like 'disabled', 'checked', and 'readonly' represent true simply by their presence on an element.

questions.question: Which meta tag instructs web crawlers NOT to index a page?
questions.explanation: <meta name="robots" content="noindex"> instructs search engine bots not to index the webpage.

questions.question: What is the correct tag for specifying Open Graph metadata (e.g. for rich previews on social media)?
questions.explanation: Open Graph uses <meta property="og:..." content="..."> tags to deliver rich preview metadata for sharing platforms.

questions.question: Which element represents the main visual container of all renderable content seen by a user in a web browser?
questions.explanation: The <body> element encloses all renderable UI components (headings, paragraphs, images, tables, etc.).

questions.question: What is an HTML attribute?
questions.b: Additional modifier information provided inside the opening tag (as name="value") to configure element behavior
questions.explanation: Attributes provide extra configuration (e.g., id, src, href) placed inside the opening tag of an element.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the <link rel="canonical" href="..."> element?
questions.a: It links an external JavaScript bundle
questions.b: It specifies the preferred authoritative URL of the webpage to prevent duplicate content SEO penalties
questions.d: It forces the browser to open links in HTTPS
questions.explanation: Canonical link tags tell search engines which URL represents the original, authoritative version of a duplicate or syndicated page.

questions.question: Which HTML tag is used to define the most important heading on a page?
questions.explanation: <h1> defines the most important heading. <h6> is the least important.

questions.question: Which tag defines a paragraph?
questions.explanation:
The

tag defines a paragraph. Browsers automatically add margin before and after a

element.

questions.question: How do you insert a single line break without starting a new paragraph?
questions.explanation:
The
tag inserts a single line break. It is an empty element.

questions.question: What is the semantic purpose of the <hr> tag in HTML5?
questions.a: To draw a purely decorative horizontal line
questions.b: To define a thematic break in the content
questions.c: To hide the text below it
questions.d: To act as a hard return for text wrapping
questions.explanation: In HTML5, <hr> represents a thematic break between paragraph-level elements, not just a visual line.

questions.question: What is the primary difference between <b> and <strong>?
questions.a: <b> makes text bigger; <strong> makes it bolder
questions.b: <b> is for styling; <strong> indicates semantic importance
questions.c: There is no difference in modern HTML
questions.explanation: Both render text bold by default, but <strong> conveys extra importance/urgency to screen readers, whereas <b> is just for visual attention.

questions.question: Which tag is used to display preformatted text, preserving both spaces and line breaks?
questions.explanation: The <pre> tag preserves both spaces and line breaks, typically rendering in a fixed-width font.

questions.question: What is the correct syntax for adding a comment in HTML?
questions.explanation: HTML comments start with <!-- and end with -->.

questions.question: Which tag defines text that has been inserted into a document (often styled with an underline)?
questions.explanation: <ins> defines inserted text. While <u> also underlines, <ins> carries semantic meaning about document edits.

questions.question: Which tag is used for subscript text, such as the '2' in H2O?
questions.explanation: <sub> defines subscript text, which appears half a character below the normal line.

questions.question: Which element defines a section that is quoted from another source?
questions.explanation: <blockquote> is used for long quotations, usually indented by browsers. <q> is for short, inline quotes.

questions.question: Which HTML tag is used to create a standard text paragraph?
questions.explanation: defines a text paragraph in HTML with standard default block margins.

questions.question: What is the highest level of section heading in HTML, typically representing the main topic of the page?
questions.explanation: <h1> denotes the most important / highest-level heading in the heading hierarchy (from h1 to h6).

questions.question: What is the semantic difference between <strong> and <b> in HTML5?
questions.b: <strong> conveys strong importance/urgency semantically, while <b> represents bold text for stylistic offset without extra importance
questions.explanation: <strong> imparts semantic importance (often spoken with emphasis by screen readers), whereas <b> applies bold styling without implying greater importance.

questions.question: What is the semantic difference between <em> and <i> in HTML5?
questions.a: <em> conveys stressed verbal emphasis, while <i> represents text in an alternate voice (idiomatic term, taxonomic name) without added emphasis
questions.b: <i> is for headers; <em> is for paragraphs
questions.d: <i> is an inline block while <em> is a block element
questions.explanation: <em> imparts stress emphasis that alters sentence meaning; <i> denotes an alternate tone or typographic offset like foreign words or scientific terms.

questions.question: Which tag is used to display superscript text (such as in mathematical exponents or footnotes: x<sup>2</sup>)?
questions.explanation: <sup> renders text as superscript (elevated with smaller font size).

questions.question: Which tag is used to display subscript text (such as in chemical formulas: H<sub>2</sub>O)?
questions.explanation: <sub> renders text as subscript (lowered with smaller font size).

questions.question: Which tag marks text that has been highlighted or marked for reference purposes (often yellow background by default)?
questions.explanation: <mark> represents text highlighted for relevance or reference in another context.

questions.question: Which semantic tag represents text that has been deleted from a document, typically rendered with a strikethrough?
questions.explanation: <del> semantically indicates deleted content, often paired with <ins> for inserted edits.

questions.question: Which semantic tag represents newly inserted or added text in a document update, rendered with an underline by default?
questions.explanation: <ins> represents content that has been added or inserted into a document.

questions.question: Which element displays text in a fixed-width monospace font while strictly preserving spaces, tabs, and line breaks exactly as typed?
questions.explanation: <pre> (preformatted text) preserves all whitespace, indentation, and newlines exactly as written in the source markup.

questions.question: Which inline element is used to denote a short fragment of computer code?
questions.explanation: <code> semantically marks an inline snippet of computer programming or script code.

questions.question: Which tag represents user keyboard input (e.g. 'Press <kbd>Ctrl</kbd> + <kbd>C</kbd>')?
questions.explanation: <kbd> represents keyboard input or user-entered keystrokes.

questions.question: Which tag is used to semantically represent sample output from a computer program or command line?
questions.explanation: <samp> represents sample or quoted output from a computer application or script.

questions.question: Which tag is used to denote a mathematical variable or program variable in HTML?
questions.explanation: <var> represents a variable in a mathematical expression or computer programming context.

questions.question: Which tag defines an abbreviation or acronym, providing the full expansion via the 'title' attribute?
questions.explanation: <abbr title="World Health Organization">WHO</abbr> provides the expansion of an acronym or abbreviation.

questions.question: Which element is used to enclose an extended quotation that is displayed as an indented block?
questions.explanation: <blockquote> is a block-level element representing content quoted from an external source.

questions.question: Which element is used for short, inline quotations that browsers automatically enclose in quotation marks?
questions.explanation: <q> defines an inline quotation; browsers automatically supply opening and closing quotation marks.

questions.question: Which semantic tag represents the title of a creative work (such as a book, movie, poem, or research paper)?
questions.explanation: <cite> marks the title of a referenced creative work (e.g. <cite>Moby Dick</cite>).

questions.question: Which element is used to provide machine-readable date/time information along with human-readable text?
questions.explanation: <time datetime="2026-08-31">August 31, 2026</time> delivers standardized machine-readable temporal data.

questions.question: What does the <wbr> (Word Break Opportunity) element specify in HTML?
questions.b: A position within a long word or URL where the browser may optionally break a line if needed to prevent layout overflow
questions.explanation: <wbr> specifies where in a long unbroken string the browser is allowed to break the line if necessary.

questions.question: Which attribute is used to apply inline CSS styles directly to an HTML element?
questions.explanation:
The 'style' attribute specifies inline CSS rules for an element (e.g.,

).

questions.question: Where should the <style> tag typically be placed for internal CSS?
questions.a: At the very end of the <body>
questions.explanation: Internal stylesheets using the <style> tag should be defined inside the <head> element.

questions.question: Which statement about the 'id' attribute is strictly true?
questions.a: An 'id' value must be unique within the entire HTML document
questions.b: Multiple elements can share the same 'id' if they are different tags
questions.c: An 'id' must begin with a number
questions.d: An 'id' cannot be used for CSS styling, only JavaScript
questions.explanation: The 'id' attribute specifies a unique identifier; no two elements on the same page can have the same id.

questions.question: How can you assign multiple classes to a single HTML element?
questions.explanation: Multiple classes are separated by a space within the same class attribute.

questions.question: Which HTML tag is used to link an external CSS stylesheet?
questions.explanation: The <link> tag (e.g., <link rel="stylesheet" href="styles.css">) is used to link external stylesheets.

questions.question: What is a 'Global Attribute' in HTML?
questions.a: An attribute that must be placed in the <html> tag
questions.b: An attribute that can be used on any HTML element
questions.c: An attribute that translates content into multiple languages
questions.d: An attribute used exclusively for geographical location data
questions.explanation: Global attributes (like class, id, style, title, lang) can be applied to almost any HTML element.

questions.question: In standard CSS specificity, which attribute takes precedence if both style an element?
questions.d: Whichever is listed first in the HTML tag
questions.explanation: An 'id' selector has higher specificity than a 'class' selector in CSS.

questions.question: Which global attribute provides a tooltip when a user hovers over an element?
questions.explanation: The 'title' attribute specifies extra information about an element, typically displayed as a tooltip on hover.

questions.question: Which attribute provides a unique identifier for a single HTML element on a webpage?
questions.explanation: The 'id' attribute must be unique across the entire HTML document.

questions.question: Which attribute is used to assign one or more reusable styling category names to an element, separated by spaces?
questions.explanation: The 'class' attribute assigns CSS class names to elements (e.g. class="btn btn-primary").

questions.question: How do you specify inline CSS styles directly on an HTML tag?
questions.explanation: The 'style' attribute specifies inline CSS property-value pairs directly on the element (e.g., style="color: red;").

questions.question: Which tag is placed in the <head> to write internal document-level CSS rules?
questions.explanation: <style> contains embedded internal CSS style sheets inside the <head> section.

questions.question: Which tag is used in <head> to link an external CSS stylesheet file to an HTML document?
questions.explanation: <link rel="stylesheet" href="styles.css"> links an external CSS stylesheet file.

questions.question: What is the standard prefix for custom data attributes in HTML5?
questions.explanation: HTML5 introduces 'data-*' attributes (e.g. data-user-id="42") to embed custom private data on elements.

questions.question: How can JavaScript access custom data attributes (like data-order-id="101") on a DOM element?
questions.explanation: The DOM 'dataset' property maps data-* attributes into camelCase JavaScript properties (e.g. dataset.orderId).

questions.question: What is the purpose of the 'title' attribute on standard HTML elements?
questions.a: It changes the webpage title tab
questions.b: It provides advisory information typically rendered as a native hover tooltip by the browser
questions.c: It acts as a primary database key
questions.d: It forces the element to render as a bold header
questions.explanation: The 'title' attribute offers extra tooltip information when the user hovers over the element with a mouse pointer.

questions.question: Which attribute specifies the text directionality of an element's content (such as left-to-right or right-to-left)?
questions.explanation: The 'dir' attribute accepts 'ltr' (left-to-right), 'rtl' (right-to-left), or 'auto'.

questions.question: What does the <bdo> (Bi-Directional Override) tag do?
questions.a: Converts text to bold italic format
questions.b: Overrides the current text direction algorithm to force a specific direction (e.g. <bdo dir="rtl">)
questions.explanation: <bdo dir="rtl"> forces text characters to render in the specified direction regardless of default unicode bidi ordering.

questions.question: What does the <bdi> (Bi-Directional Isolation) element do?
questions.a: Isolates a span of text that might be formatted in a different direction from surrounding text (e.g. user-generated Arabic names)
questions.explanation: <bdi> isolates text with unknown directionality so it does not distort neighboring text direction.

questions.question: Which global attribute makes any standard HTML element directly editable by the user in the browser?
questions.explanation: 'contenteditable="true"' turns any HTML element into a rich-text editable region.

questions.question: Which attribute controls whether browser spellchecking and grammar error detection are enabled on an element?
questions.explanation: The 'spellcheck="true|false"' attribute enables or disables native spellchecking on form fields and contenteditable elements.

questions.question: Which global attribute allows an element to be hidden from view without deleting it from the DOM structure?
questions.explanation: The boolean 'hidden' attribute instructs browsers not to render the element (analogous to display: none).

questions.question: Can an HTML element have multiple CSS class names assigned to its 'class' attribute?
questions.a: No, each element is strictly limited to 1 class name
questions.b: Yes, multiple class names are specified separated by spaces
questions.d: Only up to a maximum of 3 classes
questions.explanation: Multiple class names are combined within the class attribute separated by spaces (e.g. class="card shadow active").

questions.question: Can multiple HTML elements in the same document share the exact same 'id' attribute value?
questions.b: No, 'id' values must be unique within an HTML document to avoid invalid markup and DOM query conflicts
questions.c: Only if they are different tag types
questions.explanation: The HTML specification strictly mandates unique IDs within a document for reliable fragment linking and DOM operations.

questions.question: Which global attribute specifies an element's keyboard shortcut activation key?
questions.explanation: The 'accesskey' attribute defines a keyboard shortcut to activate or focus an element (e.g., accesskey="s").

questions.question: What is the purpose of the 'nonce' attribute on <style> or <script> tags in modern web security?
questions.b: It provides a cryptographic one-time token verified by Content Security Policy (CSP) headers before execution
questions.explanation: A 'nonce' (number used once) allows CSP-compliant browsers to verify that an inline script or style was authorized by the server.

questions.question: Which attribute specifies that an external stylesheet is intended specifically for print output media?
questions.explanation: The 'media' attribute on <link> (e.g. media="print") restricts stylesheet application to print dialogs and print rendering.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the <template> element in HTML5?
questions.a: It renders a predefined boilerplate layout immediately
questions.b: It holds client-side HTML content that is not rendered on page load, but can be cloned and instantiated at runtime via JavaScript
questions.c: It compiles Markdown to HTML on the fly
questions.d: It downloads external HTML files automatically
questions.explanation: <template> contains hidden inert markup used as a blueprint for dynamic component rendering in JavaScript.

questions.question: What is the <slot> element used for in modern Web Components?
questions.a: Allocating heap memory for Web Workers
questions.b: Acting as a placeholder inside a shadow DOM tree where external consumer markup is projected/slotted
questions.c: Creating grid slots in CSS Grid
questions.explanation: <slot> defines placeholders inside Shadow DOM components into which user-provided markup is rendered.

questions.question: What is the effect of setting 'translate="no"' on an HTML element?
questions.b: Instructs automated translation tools (like Google Translate) not to translate the element's text content
questions.explanation: The 'translate="no"' attribute tells automated translation systems (like browser translation features) to leave brand names or code untranslated.

questions.question: Which tag is used to create a hyperlink?
questions.explanation: The <a> (anchor) tag is used to define a hyperlink to another page or resource.

questions.question: Which attribute of the <a> tag indicates the link's destination?
questions.explanation: The 'href' (Hypertext Reference) attribute contains the URL destination of the link.

questions.question: How do you make a link open in a new tab or window?
questions.explanation: Setting target="_blank" forces the browser to open the linked document in a new tab or window.

questions.question: What happens when the href attribute contains a value like href="#contact"?
questions.a: It throws an invalid URL error
questions.b: It links to a page named contact.html
questions.c: It jumps to the element on the same page with id="contact"
questions.d: It opens a new email draft to 'contact'
questions.explanation: The hash symbol (#) creates a bookmark link, jumping to the element with that specific id on the current page.

questions.question: Which href value creates a link that opens the user's default email client?
questions.explanation: The 'mailto:' scheme inside an href opens the user's email program to send a message to that address.

questions.question: What is the difference between an absolute URL and a relative URL?
questions.a: Absolute URLs only work on the internet; relative URLs only work locally
questions.b: Absolute URLs include the full web address (e.g., https://...); relative URLs point to a file within the same site
questions.c: Absolute URLs are for images; relative URLs are for text
questions.explanation: Absolute URLs contain the protocol and domain. Relative URLs describe the path relative to the current file structure.

questions.question: By default, how do web browsers visually represent an unvisited link?
questions.explanation: The standard browser default for an unvisited link is underlined blue text. Visited links become purple.

questions.question: How do you use an image as a link?
questions.explanation: You nest the tag inside the tag to make the image clickable.

questions.question: Which tag is used to create a hyperlink in HTML?
questions.explanation: The <a> (anchor) tag creates hyperlinks connecting to other webpages, files, email addresses, or document locations.

questions.question: Which attribute on the <a> tag specifies the destination URL or target address of a hyperlink?
questions.explanation: The 'href' (Hypertext REFerence) attribute specifies the destination URL of the link.

questions.question: How do you create an email link that automatically opens the user's default email client?
questions.explanation: The 'mailto:' URL scheme instructs the operating system to launch the default email client with the specified recipient.

questions.question: How do you create a clickable telephone link that dials a phone number on mobile devices?
questions.explanation: The 'tel:' URL scheme creates a clickable telephone link on smartphones and VoIP dialers.

questions.question: How do you link directly to a specific section of the same page that has 'id="section2"'?
questions.explanation: Hyperlink hashes (e.g. href="#section2") scroll directly to the element whose id equals 'section2'.

questions.question: Which value for the 'target' attribute opens a linked document in a new tab or window?
questions.explanation: target="_blank" instructs the browser to open the link in a new browser tab or separate window.

questions.question: Why should links opening in target="_blank" always include 'rel="noopener noreferrer"' (or rely on modern defaults)?
questions.b: To prevent the newly opened page from accessing 'window.opener' and maliciously manipulating the origin tab
questions.explanation: 'noopener' prevents the target page from obtaining a reference to the referring window, mitigating reverse tab-nabbing security vulnerabilities.

questions.question: Which attribute on an <a> tag prompts the browser to download the linked resource rather than navigating to it?
questions.explanation: The 'download' attribute prompts file downloading and optionally specifies the default saved filename (e.g. download="report.pdf").

questions.question: What is the default value of the 'target' attribute if omitted on an <a> tag?
questions.explanation: target="_self" is the default, opening the linked resource in the same browsing context/frame.

questions.question: What does target="_parent" do when clicked inside a nested <iframe>?
questions.a: Opens the link in a new browser window
questions.b: Opens the link in the immediate parent frame of the current frame
questions.c: Opens the link on the server
questions.explanation: target="_parent" navigates the immediate parent browsing context containing the iframe.

questions.question: What does target="_top" do?
questions.a: Scrolls to the top of the current page
questions.b: Opens the linked document in the topmost window of the entire frame hierarchy, breaking out of all nested iframes
questions.c: Pins the link to the browser bookmark bar
questions.d: Opens the link with highest priority
questions.explanation: target="_top" breaks out of any nested frame hierarchy and loads the page across the entire browser viewport.

questions.question: What is the purpose of 'rel="nofollow"' on a hyperlink?
questions.b: It tells search engine crawlers not to follow the link or transfer SEO link equity / ranking signals
questions.d: It forces the link to load over FTP
questions.explanation: rel="nofollow" indicates that the author does not endorse the target URL, preventing search bots from passing ranking reputation.

questions.question: What does 'rel="sponsored"' signify in modern SEO link markup?
questions.a: The link represents an academic citation
questions.b: The link was created as part of a paid advertising or sponsorship arrangement
questions.c: The link is hosted on a government server
questions.d: The link offers free software downloads
questions.explanation: Google and standard engines use rel="sponsored" to designate paid commercial or sponsored hyperlinks.

questions.question: What does 'rel="ugc"' indicate on an anchor element?
questions.b: User Generated Content (e.g. comments, forum posts) to distinguish user-submitted links from editorial content
questions.explanation: rel="ugc" indicates User-Generated Content links posted by site visitors in comment sections or forum threads.

questions.question: What is the difference between an absolute URL and a relative URL in an href attribute?
questions.a: Absolute URLs include the full protocol and domain (e.g. https://site.com/page); relative URLs are relative to the current path (e.g. /about.html)
questions.b: Relative URLs only work with images
questions.c: Absolute URLs cannot contain query parameters
questions.d: Relative URLs are only used in local intranet environments
questions.explanation: Absolute URLs define complete web addresses including protocol and domain; relative URLs resolve relative to the current document origin or path.

questions.question: How do you link to an SMS text message on mobile devices?
questions.explanation: The 'sms:' URI scheme opens the native mobile messaging app with the target phone number prepopulated.

questions.question: Which attribute specifies the MIME type of the destination resource linked by an <a> or <link> tag?
questions.explanation: The 'type' attribute provides an advisory MIME type (e.g., type="application/pdf") of the linked resource.

questions.question: What does an anchor with 'href="javascript:void(0);"' do when clicked?
questions.b: Prevents page reload and URL fragment changes while allowing JavaScript click listeners to handle the event
questions.explanation: 'javascript:void(0);' evaluates to undefined, preventing browser navigation when triggering JavaScript actions.

questions.question: Can an entire <div> containing headings and images be wrapped inside a single <a> element in HTML5?
questions.a: No, anchors can only enclose inline text elements in HTML5
questions.b: Yes, HTML5 explicitly permits <a> elements to wrap block-level content (like divs, articles, and cards)
questions.c: Only if the div has display: inline
questions.explanation: HTML5 permits <a> tags to wrap flow content, making entire cards, divs, and complex UI blocks clickable hyperlinks.

questions.question: What does 'hreflang' attribute on an <a> tag specify?
questions.a: The programming language of the backend server
questions.b: The human language of the linked destination document (e.g. hreflang="es")
questions.c: The font character encoding of the link text
questions.explanation: The 'hreflang' attribute indicates the natural language of the target document.

questions.question: What is the purpose of 'rel="prefetch"' on a <link> element?
questions.b: It hints to the browser to download and cache a resource in the background during idle time because the user is likely to visit it next
questions.c: It renders the resource in a hidden background tab
questions.d: It forces synchronous blocking download of scripts
questions.explanation: 'rel="prefetch"' is a low-priority resource hint that fetches assets needed for future navigations during browser idle time.

questions.question: What is the purpose of 'rel="preload"' on a <link> element?
questions.a: It delays asset downloading until page scroll
questions.b: It informs the browser to fetch a critical resource (such as fonts or key CSS/hero images) as early as possible with high priority
questions.c: It creates a backup mirror of the HTML page
questions.explanation: 'rel="preload"' forces immediate, high-priority discovery and downloading of critical assets needed for current page rendering.

questions.question: Which attribute is required to specify the path to the image in an tag?
questions.explanation: The 'src' (source) attribute specifies the path or URL to the image file.

questions.question: Why is the 'alt' attribute crucial for images?
questions.a: It makes the image load faster
questions.b: It provides alternative text if the image fails to load and for screen readers
questions.explanation: The 'alt' attribute provides semantic meaning for accessibility (screen readers) and acts as a visual fallback if the network fails.

questions.question: What happens if you define both 'width' and 'height' attributes on an tag?
questions.a: The browser reserves space for the image before it loads, preventing layout shifts
questions.b: The browser overrides CSS rules associated with the image
questions.c: The image is automatically compressed in file size
questions.d: The image becomes responsive to the screen width
questions.explanation: Setting width and height attributes reserves the correct layout space, preventing Cumulative Layout Shift (CLS) as the page loads.

questions.question: Which tag allows you to specify different image sources depending on the user's screen size or format support?
questions.explanation: The <picture> element works with <source> child elements to provide art direction (different crops for mobile vs desktop) or format switching (e.g., WebP vs JPEG).

questions.question: Inside a <picture> element, which tag is used to specify the alternative media files?
questions.explanation: The <source> element is used inside <picture> (and <audio>/<video>) to specify media resources and their media queries/types.

questions.question: Which attribute delays the loading of an image until it is close to the viewport?
questions.explanation: The loading="lazy" attribute instructs the browser to defer loading the image until it enters or is about to enter the visible viewport.

questions.question: How do you add a favicon to a website?
questions.explanation: Favicons are added in the <head> using the <link> tag with rel="icon".

questions.question: What is an HTML Image Map?
questions.a: An image generated dynamically via JavaScript
questions.b: An image with clickable areas linking to different destinations
questions.c: A map embedded from Google Maps
questions.d: An SVG image that scales infinitely
questions.explanation: Image maps (using <map> and <area> tags) define clickable regions (coords) over a single image.

questions.question: Which attribute links an to a element?
questions.explanation: The 'usemap' attribute on the tag points to the 'name' attribute of a element (e.g., usemap="#planetmap").

questions.question: Is an image defined via CSS 'background-image' read by screen readers by default?
questions.a: Yes, screen readers analyze all background images
questions.b: No, background images are strictly decorative and ignored by screen readers
questions.c: Yes, but only if the filename is descriptive
questions.d: No, unless an alt attribute is added to the CSS
questions.explanation: CSS background images are treated as visual decoration. If an image contains crucial information, an HTML tag with an 'alt' attribute must be used.

questions.question: Which tag is used to embed an image into an HTML document?
questions.explanation: The tag embeds raster or vector images into an HTML document.

questions.question: Which attribute specifies the image file path or URL on an tag?
questions.explanation: The 'src' (source) attribute provides the location URL of the image file.

questions.question: Why is the 'alt' attribute essential on all elements?
questions.a: It is required for CSS animations
questions.b: It provides alternative text for screen readers (accessibility) and displays if the image fails to load
questions.c: It specifies image dimensions in pixels
questions.d: It increases image resolution on retina screens
questions.explanation: The 'alt' text is vital for visually impaired users using screen readers and acts as fallback text on broken image paths.

questions.question: What should you set alt="" to when an image is purely decorative (e.g. background flourishes)?
questions.b: Set an empty alt attribute (alt="") so screen readers know to skip the decorative image safely
questions.explanation: An empty 'alt=""' tells assistive screen readers that the graphic is decorative and should be silently ignored.

questions.question: Why is it best practice to specify explicit 'width' and 'height' attributes on tags?
questions.a: To force the browser to crop the image
questions.b: To allow the browser to calculate aspect ratio and allocate layout space before the image loads, preventing Cumulative Layout Shift (CLS)
questions.c: To compress image bytes on the server
questions.d: To convert PNG files to SVG automatically
questions.explanation: Explicit width/height attributes provide aspect ratios, allowing the browser to reserve layout space and eliminate layout shifts.

questions.question: Which attribute enables native lazy loading of images in modern browsers without JavaScript libraries?
questions.explanation: 'loading="lazy"' defers loading off-screen images until the user scrolls near them.

questions.question: What does the 'loading="eager"' attribute do on an image?
questions.a: Loads the image only on hover
questions.b: Instructs the browser to load the image immediately without deferral regardless of scroll position
questions.explanation: loading="eager" tells the browser to fetch the image immediately upon parsing (ideal for above-the-fold hero images).

questions.question: Which HTML5 container element groups an image/media along with its caption?
questions.explanation: <figure> represents self-contained content (like diagrams or photos) typically referenced with a caption.

questions.question: Which tag is used inside a <figure> element to define the human-readable caption for that figure?
questions.explanation: <figcaption> defines the caption or legend associated with its parent <figure> element.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the <picture> element in HTML5 responsive design?
questions.a: It generates thumbnail previews with WebGL
questions.b: It provides multiple <source> options based on media queries or image formats (WebP/AVIF), allowing the browser to choose the best fit
questions.c: It acts as a photo gallery carousel
questions.explanation: <picture> enables art direction and format switching (e.g. serving AVIF/WebP with JPG fallback) based on device capabilities.

questions.question: Which attribute on allows supplying a list of image files with pixel densities (1x, 2x) or intrinsic widths (e.g. 800w)?
questions.explanation: The 'srcset' attribute provides candidate image URLs mapped to pixel densities or display widths.

questions.question: Which attribute works alongside 'srcset' to tell the browser how wide the image will display under different media query conditions?
questions.explanation: The 'sizes' attribute defines the intended display width of the image at various viewport breakpoints.

questions.question: What is an HTML Image Map created with the <map> and <area> tags?
questions.b: An image with clickable coordinate regions (rect, circle, poly) linking to different destinations
questions.c: A site map diagram generated with SVG
questions.explanation: <map name="..."> paired with <area shape="..." coords="..."> defines clickable geometric hotspot regions on an image.

questions.question: Which attribute connects an tag to a corresponding element?
questions.explanation: The 'usemap="#workmap"' attribute links the image to the specified coordinate map name.

questions.question: What attribute hint informs the browser about the download priority of a critical above-the-fold hero image?
questions.explanation: fetchpriority="high" signals to the browser's preload scanner that the image has high relative fetch priority.

questions.question: What is a Base64 Data URI used in an image 'src' attribute (e.g. 'data:image/png;base64,...')?
questions.b: An inline string representation of binary image data embedded directly into the HTML without a separate HTTP request
questions.explanation: Data URIs encode raw image bytes into ASCII base64 text, embedding small icons or graphics directly in HTML/CSS.

questions.question: Which image format natively supports lossy and lossless compression with alpha transparency and superior compression over PNG/JPEG?
questions.explanation: WebP provides modern 24-bit color, lossless/lossy compression, and alpha transparency with significantly smaller payloads than PNG/JPEG.

questions.question: Which cutting-edge image format based on AV1 video codec offers even higher compression efficiency than WebP?
questions.explanation: AVIF (AV1 Image File Format) offers exceptional compression ratios and wide color gamut support for modern web pages.

questions.question: What does the 'decoding="async"' attribute do on an element?
questions.a: Decodes the image asynchronously off the main thread to prevent blocking page rendering and user scrolling
questions.explanation: decoding="async" allows image rasterization to take place off the main UI thread, avoiding scroll judder.

questions.question: What does the 'crossorigin' attribute (e.g. crossorigin="anonymous") configure on an element?
questions.a: It allows sharing the image on social media
questions.b: It configures Cross-Origin Resource Sharing (CORS) credentials for loading images from external domains for use with Canvas API
questions.c: It forces the image to load over HTTP
questions.explanation: 'crossorigin' controls CORS requests, preventing canvas tainting when manipulating third-party images in WebGL / 2D canvas.

questions.question: Which tag defines an HTML table?
questions.explanation: The <table> tag is the container for all other table elements like rows and data cells.

questions.question: Which tag is used to define a standard data cell in a table?
questions.explanation: The <td> (table data) tag defines a standard cell containing data within a table row.

questions.question: What is the visual difference between a <th> and a <td> element by default?
questions.b: <th> text is bold and centered; <td> is normal and left-aligned
questions.c: <th> cells have borders; <td> cells do not
questions.d: There is no default visual difference
questions.explanation: Browsers render <th> (table header) text as bold and centered to distinguish it from regular <td> data.

questions.question: Which attribute allows a single table cell to span across multiple columns?
questions.explanation: The 'colspan' attribute (e.g., <td colspan="2">) merges adjacent cells horizontally across columns.

questions.question: Which attribute allows a table cell to span across multiple rows?
questions.explanation: The 'rowspan' attribute allows a single cell to stretch vertically across multiple rows.

questions.question: Which HTML tag is used to add a title or explanation above an HTML table?
questions.explanation: The <caption> tag must be inserted immediately after the <table> tag and provides a title for the table.

questions.question: What are the correct tags to group the header, body, and footer content of a table?
questions.explanation: <thead>, <tbody>, and <tfoot> group table rows semantically, which is useful for CSS styling and printing long tables across pages.

questions.question: Is it possible to nest another complete <table> inside a <td> element?
questions.a: Yes, HTML allows tables to be nested inside table data cells
questions.b: No, nesting tables invalidates the HTML structure
questions.c: Yes, but only if the nested table has no <th> elements
questions.d: No, tables can only be nested inside <div> elements
questions.explanation: Table data cells (<td>) can contain almost any HTML element, including entire nested tables.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the <colgroup> and <col> elements?
questions.a: To group columns together for shared CSS styling without applying styles to every cell
questions.b: To merge columns together like the colspan attribute
questions.c: To define the data type (text, number, date) of a column
questions.d: To make columns responsive and collapse on mobile devices
questions.explanation: <colgroup> specifies a group of one or more columns (<col>) for formatting. It prevents having to repeat CSS classes on every <td>.

questions.question: How does the 'scope' attribute improve table accessibility?
questions.a: It highlights the active cell for screen readers
questions.b: It tells screen readers if a <th> is a header for a row, column, row group, or col group
questions.c: It forces the table to fit within the viewport scope
questions.d: It links a table caption to a specific cell
questions.explanation: Using scope="col" or scope="row" on a <th> element explicitly associates the header with its corresponding data cells for assistive technologies.

questions.question: Which HTML tag is used to create a table structure?
questions.explanation: The <table> element defines an HTML table for displaying structured tabular data.

questions.question: Which tag defines an individual row within an HTML table?
questions.explanation: <tr> (Table Row) defines a horizontal row of cells in a table.

questions.question: Which tag is used to create a standard data cell inside a table row?
questions.explanation: <td> (Table Data) defines a standard data cell inside a table row.

questions.question: Which tag is used to define a header cell in a table, rendering text bold and centered by default?
questions.explanation: <th> (Table Header) defines a column or row header cell, visually styled as bold and centered.

questions.question: Which attribute allows a table cell to stretch horizontally across multiple columns?
questions.explanation: The 'colspan' attribute (e.g. <td colspan="3">) spans a cell across multiple columns.

questions.question: Which element encapsulates the header rows of a table to separate them from data body rows?
questions.explanation: <thead> groups the header rows at the top of an HTML table.

questions.question: Which element groups the primary body content rows of a table?
questions.explanation: <tbody> encapsulates the main data rows of a table.

questions.question: Which element groups the summary or footer rows at the bottom of a table?
questions.explanation: <tfoot> defines the footer summary section of a table.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the <caption> element in an HTML table?
questions.a: To add a tooltip hover description
questions.b: To specify an accessible title or description displayed directly above or below the table
questions.explanation: <caption> placed as the first child of <table> specifies the official title and description of the table.

questions.question: What is the function of the <colgroup> and <col> elements?
questions.b: They allow applying styles (such as background colors and widths) across entire vertical columns at once without repeating styles on every td
questions.d: They convert tables to CSV format
questions.explanation: <colgroup> and <col span="2"> apply structural formatting and CSS styles across whole columns simultaneously.

questions.question: What are the standard values for the 'scope' attribute on <th> elements?
questions.explanation: scope="col|row|colgroup|rowgroup" defines whether a header cell applies to a column, row, or grouping for screen readers.

questions.question: Which attribute on a <td> cell can reference the 'id' of its corresponding <th> headers for complex multi-level tables?
questions.explanation: The 'headers' attribute on <td> specifies a space-separated list of <th> IDs to associate data cells with multiple headers.

questions.question: Why should HTML <table> elements NEVER be used for page layout and grid design in modern web development?
questions.b: Tables destroy accessibility, degrade screen reader navigation, and make responsive design extremely difficult compared to CSS Flexbox/Grid
questions.explanation: Using tables for page layout ruins semantic structure, confuses screen readers, and harms responsive mobile presentation.

questions.question: How does the 'span' attribute work on a <col> element?
questions.a: Spans a column across multiple tables
questions.b: Specifies the number of consecutive columns that share the styling of that <col> element
questions.c: Converts the column to inline span format
questions.explanation: <col span="3" style="background-color: yellow;"> applies the background color to the next 3 consecutive columns.

questions.question: What CSS property is commonly used to remove default double borders between adjacent table cells?
questions.explanation: 'border-collapse: collapse;' merges adjacent cell borders into a single clean border in CSS.

questions.question: What does 'table-layout: fixed;' do in CSS when applied to an HTML <table>?
questions.a: Fixes the table to the top of the viewport
questions.b: Calculates column widths based on the first row's widths rather than parsing the content of every cell, speeding up table rendering
questions.explanation: 'table-layout: fixed' enforces fast layout determination from column/header widths without scanning the whole dataset.

questions.question: Can an HTML <table> contain multiple <tbody> elements?
questions.a: No, only one <tbody> is permitted per table
questions.b: Yes, multiple <tbody> elements can be used to divide large tables into distinct logical data blocks
questions.c: Only if each tbody has a different color
questions.explanation: Multiple <tbody> tags are valid in a single table, allowing developers to group separate sections of rows for styling or scrolling.

questions.question: Where should the <caption> tag be placed inside a <table> definition?
questions.b: As the very first element directly following the opening <table> tag
questions.explanation: Per HTML standards, if <caption> is used, it must be the immediate first child of the <table> element.

questions.question: What is the default text alignment for <td> vs <th> elements in standard browser user agent stylesheets?
questions.a: <td> is left-aligned regular; <th> is centered bold
questions.explanation: User agent stylesheets default <td> to left-aligned regular weight and <th> to centered bold text.

questions.question: How do you make an HTML table horizontally scrollable on small mobile screens without breaking page width?
questions.b: Wrap the <table> in a container <div> with CSS 'overflow-x: auto;'
questions.explanation: Wrapping tables in <div style="overflow-x: auto;"> allows wide tables to scroll smoothly on narrow mobile screens.

questions.question: Which tag creates a bulleted (unordered) list?
questions.explanation: The <ul> (unordered list) tag creates a list where items are typically marked with bullets.

questions.question: Which tag creates a numbered (ordered) list?
questions.explanation: The <ol> (ordered list) tag creates a list where items are marked with numbers or letters.

questions.question: Which tag is used to define an individual item within both <ul> and <ol> lists?
questions.explanation: The <li> tag defines a list item.

questions.question: How do you change an ordered list to use uppercase Roman numerals (I, II, III)?
questions.explanation: The type attribute on an <ol> (e.g., type="I", type="a", type="1") changes the numbering marker.

questions.question: Which attribute allows an ordered list to begin counting from a number other than 1?
questions.explanation: The 'start' attribute specifies the numeric starting value of an ordered list (e.g., <ol start="50">).

questions.question: How do you make an ordered list count downwards (3, 2, 1)?
questions.explanation: The boolean attribute 'reversed' specifies that the list order should be descending.

questions.question: Which three tags are required to create a description list (like a dictionary)?
questions.explanation: <dl> defines the description list, <dt> defines the term, and <dd> describes/defines the term.

questions.question: What is the fundamental layout difference between <div> and <span>?
questions.a: <div> is for text; <span> is for images
questions.b: <div> is an inline element; <span> is a block-level element
questions.c: <div> is a block-level element; <span> is an inline element
questions.d: There is no difference; they are interchangeable
questions.explanation: <div> always starts on a new line and takes up full width (block). <span> does not start a new line and only takes up necessary width (inline).

questions.question: What does <ul> stand for in HTML?
questions.explanation: <ul> defines an Unordered (bulleted) List.

questions.question: What does <ol> stand for in HTML?
questions.explanation: <ol> defines an Ordered (numbered/sequential) List.

questions.question: What does <li> stand for?
questions.explanation: <li> defines an individual List Item inside <ul>, <ol>, or <menu>.

questions.question: Which tag defines a Description List (formerly Definition List) in HTML?
questions.explanation: <dl> (Description List) encloses terms and their corresponding descriptions.

questions.question: Which tag defines the description term (name/key) inside a <dl> list?
questions.explanation: <dt> (Description Term) defines the term being defined in a description list.

questions.question: Which tag defines the description data (definition/value) inside a <dl> list?
questions.explanation: <dd> (Description Details/Data) provides the definition or description for the preceding <dt> term.

questions.question: Can a single <dt> term in a <dl> list have multiple associated <dd> description elements?
questions.b: Yes, one term can have multiple definitions, and multiple terms can share a single definition
questions.explanation: HTML description lists support 1:many and many:many relationships between <dt> terms and <dd> descriptions.

questions.question: Which attribute sets an ordered list to use lowercase alphabetical letters (a, b, c)?
questions.explanation: The 'type="a"' attribute on <ol> specifies lowercase alphabetical numbering (a, b, c...).

questions.question: Which attribute sets an ordered list to use uppercase alphabetical letters (A, B, C)?
questions.explanation: type="A" on <ol> numbers list items with uppercase letters (A, B, C...).

questions.question: Which attribute sets an ordered list to use lowercase Roman numerals (i, ii, iii)?
questions.explanation: type="i" produces lowercase Roman numerals.

questions.question: Which attribute on <ol> reverses the numbering sequence (e.g. counting down from 10 to 1)?
questions.explanation: The boolean 'reversed' attribute numbers ordered list items in descending order.

questions.question: Which attribute on an individual <li> item within an <ol> overrides its ordinal number value?
questions.explanation: The 'value' attribute on <li> (e.g. <li value="50">) changes the ordinal numbering for that and subsequent items.

questions.question: How do you create a nested list (a sub-list inside a list item)?
questions.a: Place a <ul> or <ol> directly inside an existing <li> element
questions.b: Place a <ul> between two <li> items without wrapping
questions.explanation: To nest lists validly in HTML, the entire child <ul> or <ol> must be placed inside a parent <li> container.

questions.question: What is the primary role of the generic <div> element in HTML?
questions.a: To define a mathematical division operation
questions.b: To act as a generic block-level container for grouping elements and applying CSS styles or scripts without inherent semantic meaning
questions.explanation: <div> is a generic block container without semantic meaning, used for grouping, styling, and layout structure.

questions.question: What is the primary role of the generic <span> element in HTML?
questions.a: To span across multiple table rows
questions.b: To act as a generic inline container for styling or scripting a specific portion of text without breaking the line
questions.explanation: <span> is a generic inline element used to style or script text segments without altering line flow.

questions.question: What is the <hr> element in modern HTML5 semantically defined as?
questions.b: A thematic break or shift of topic between paragraph-level elements
questions.explanation: HTML5 defines <hr> as a semantic thematic break between paragraph-level topics.

questions.question:
What does the
tag do in an HTML document?
questions.b: Produces a line break (carriage return) within text flow without creating a new paragraph
questions.explanation: produces a line break within text (e.g. for poems or postal addresses).

questions.question: What is the <menu> element in modern HTML5?
questions.b: A semantic alternative to <ul> for representing an unordered list of interactive items / menu commands
questions.explanation: In modern HTML5, <menu> is a semantic alternative to <ul> specifically intended for lists of interactive toolbar/menu options.

questions.question: Can <div> elements be placed directly inside a <dl> description list in modern HTML5.2+?
questions.a: No, dl can only contain dt and dd directly
questions.b: Yes, <div> wrappers are explicitly allowed inside <dl> to group <dt> and <dd> pairs for CSS styling (like flexbox/grid layouts)
questions.explanation: HTML5.2 updated the <dl> content model to allow <div> wrappers around <dt>/<dd> groups for flexbox and grid styling.

questions.question: Which CSS property is standardly used to change or remove list bullet markers (e.g. list-style-type: none)?
questions.explanation: 'list-style-type: none;' removes bullet points from <ul> or <ol> list items in CSS.

questions.question: What is the semantic purpose of the <address> element?
questions.b: To supply contact information for the author or owner of the document or nearest article ancestor
questions.c: To format street addresses for postal printing only
questions.d: To specify IP addresses in network logs
questions.explanation: <address> indicates contact information (email, phone, URL, physical address) for the document author or organization.

questions.question:
Why should
tags NOT be used repeatedly to create vertical spacing between paragraphs?
questions.b: It ruins responsive typography and breaks screen reader paragraph navigation; CSS margins should be used instead
questions.c: It forces the page to reload
questions.explanation:
Spacing should be handled via CSS margin/padding properties, not repeated empty
line breaks.

questions.question: What does 'Semantic HTML' mean?
questions.a: Using HTML tags that describe the meaning of the content, not just its appearance
questions.b: Using HTML combined with a semantic CSS framework like Bootstrap
questions.c: Writing HTML in strict alphabetical order
questions.d: Creating HTML pages that are entirely accessible without CSS
questions.explanation: Semantic HTML elements (like <header>, <article>, <form>) clearly describe their meaning to both the browser and the developer.

questions.question: Which semantic element is typically used to group introductory content or a set of navigational links at the top of a page?
questions.explanation: The <header> element represents a container for introductory content or a set of navigational links.

questions.question: Which tag should wrap a block of major navigation links on a website?
questions.explanation: The <nav> element defines a set of navigation links. It is intended only for major blocks of navigation.

questions.question: Which tag represents content that is tangentially related to the content around it, often displayed as a sidebar?
questions.explanation: The <aside> element is used for content loosely related to the primary content, such as sidebars, pull quotes, or ads.

questions.question: What is the correct semantic element for a self-contained composition in a document, such as a blog post or news story?
questions.explanation: The <article> element specifies independent, self-contained content that should make sense on its own (e.g., a forum post or news article).

questions.question: What distinguishes the <main> element from other semantic tags like <section> or <article>?
questions.a: It automatically centers content on the screen
questions.b: There should only be one visible <main> element per document
questions.d: It replaces the <body> element in HTML5
questions.explanation: The <main> tag specifies the dominant content of the <body>. A document must not have more than one <main> element visible.

questions.question: Which element defines the authorship, copyright, or contact information for its nearest sectioning element or page?
questions.explanation: The <footer> element typically contains authorship information, copyright data, and related documents links.

questions.question: When should you use a <section> element instead of a <div>?
questions.a: When the content needs a border
questions.b: When the content represents a thematic grouping usually with its own heading
questions.c: When the content contains forms or inputs
questions.d: When you want the content to be inline rather than block-level
questions.explanation: <section> is a semantic block for a thematic grouping of content (typically with a heading). <div> has no semantic meaning and is strictly for styling/layout.

questions.question: Which two tags work together to create an interactive 'accordion' widget that users can click to open and close?
questions.explanation: <details> creates an interactive widget that the user can open/close. <summary> provides the visible heading that the user clicks.

questions.question: How do semantic layout elements directly benefit SEO (Search Engine Optimization)?
questions.a: They execute faster in the browser engine
questions.b: They help search engines understand the structure, context, and hierarchy of the content
questions.c: They hide keywords from users while showing them to search bots
questions.explanation: Search engines use semantic tags to better index the page by understanding which parts are navigation, main content, or side notes.

questions.question: Which semantic element represents the major navigation block containing hyperlinks to other pages or sections?
questions.explanation: <nav> designates a major section of navigation links on a website.

questions.question: Which semantic tag represents introductory content, site logos, search forms, and navigation at the top of a page or article?
questions.explanation: <header> contains introductory content, site mastheads, or headings for a page or article.

questions.question: Which semantic element represents the dominant central content unique to the document (only one visible instance per page)?
questions.explanation: <main> encloses the unique central content of the document, excluding repeated headers, footers, and sidebars.

questions.question: Which element represents a self-contained, independently distributable composition (such as a blog post, forum post, or product card)?
questions.explanation: <article> represents a self-contained composition suitable for independent syndication (e.g. RSS feeds, news items).

questions.question: Which element represents a standalone thematic section of content, typically introduced by a heading?
questions.explanation: <section> groups thematically related content that typically includes a heading element (h1-h6).

questions.question: Which element is used to represent content tangentially related to the main content (such as sidebars, pull quotes, or related links)?
questions.explanation: <aside> represents content indirectly related to the primary text, commonly rendered as a sidebar or callout box.

questions.question: Which semantic element defines the footer for its nearest sectioning ancestor or page (containing copyright, legal notices, etc.)?
questions.explanation: <footer> contains concluding information, author details, copyright notices, and sitemap links.

questions.question: Which HTML5 element creates a native disclosure widget that the user can expand or collapse by clicking?
questions.explanation: <details> creates an interactive open/close toggle widget natively without requiring JavaScript.

questions.question: Which tag is used as the first child of <details> to define the visible clickable heading of the disclosure widget?
questions.explanation: <summary> provides the visible label/heading for a <details> disclosure toggle.

questions.question: Which boolean attribute on <details> makes it open by default on page load?
questions.explanation: The 'open' attribute on <details> causes the disclosure widget to display in its open/expanded state on load.

questions.question: Which element represents a modal or non-modal popup dialog box or window in modern HTML5?
questions.explanation: <dialog> is the standard HTML5 element for accessible native dialog boxes and modals.

questions.question: What JavaScript method on the HTMLDialogElement opens a <dialog> as a true modal with background backdrop dimming and focus trapping?
questions.explanation: 'dialog.showModal()' opens the dialog as a modal, activating the ::backdrop pseudo-element and restricting focus.

questions.question: What JavaScript method closes an open <dialog> element?
questions.explanation: 'dialog.close()' closes the dialog and removes it from the top-layer stack.

questions.question: Which CSS pseudo-element allows styling the backdrop overlay behind a modal opened with dialog.showModal()?
questions.explanation: The '::backdrop' CSS pseudo-element styles the full-screen overlay behind active top-layer modal dialogs.

questions.question: What is the <hgroup> element used for in HTML5.3?
questions.b:
Grouping an

-

heading with associated subtitles, taglines, or

summaries
questions.explanation: <hgroup> groups a heading (h1-h6) together with auxiliary subheadings, subtitles, or paragraphs.

questions.question: What is the difference between <head> and <header> in HTML?
questions.a: <head> contains non-visible metadata and resource links; <header> contains visible UI layout introductory content inside <body>
questions.c: <header> is used only for text headers inside tables
questions.d: They are completely identical in function
questions.explanation: <head> houses document metadata (title, meta, styles); <header> is a visible structural container inside <body>.

questions.question: What landmark role does the <main> element map to by default in assistive technologies?
questions.explanation: <main> inherently maps to the ARIA role 'main', allowing screen reader users to jump straight to main content.

questions.question: What landmark role does the <header> element map to when scoped directly to <body>?
questions.explanation: A top-level <header> scoped to <body> implicitly has the ARIA landmark role 'banner'.

questions.question: What landmark role does the <footer> element map to when scoped directly to <body>?
questions.explanation: A page-level <footer> maps to ARIA role 'contentinfo'.

questions.question: What landmark role does the <aside> element map to?
questions.explanation: <aside> maps directly to the ARIA landmark role 'complementary'.

questions.question: Which HTML element is used to create a document section containing interactive controls for submitting information?
questions.explanation: The <form> tag defines a form that is used to collect user input.

questions.question: Which attribute of the <form> tag specifies the URL where the form data should be sent?
questions.explanation: The 'action' attribute specifies the URL/URI of the file or server endpoint that processes the submitted form data.

questions.question: Which form method appends form data directly into the URL as name/value pairs?
questions.explanation: The GET method appends the form data to the URL (e.g., /page?name=john). It is not secure for sensitive data.

questions.question: Why should the POST method always be used when sending passwords or sensitive data?
questions.a: Because POST data is encrypted by the browser automatically
questions.b: Because POST sends data in the HTTP request body, keeping it out of browser history and URLs
questions.d: Because POST data cannot be intercepted by hackers
questions.explanation: POST appends form data inside the body of the HTTP request, preventing sensitive info from being visible in the URL, bookmarks, or browser history.

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of the <label> element?
questions.a: To make text bold and red next to a form input
questions.b: To group multiple form fields together inside a box
questions.c: To define a clickable text label linked to a specific form control, improving usability
questions.d: To validate the data entered by the user
questions.explanation: Labels improve accessibility and usability. Clicking a linked <label> automatically focuses its associated form input.

questions.question: How do you correctly bind a <label> to a specific <input> element?
questions.a: The <label> 'for' attribute must match the <input> 'name' attribute
questions.b: The <label> 'for' attribute must match the <input> 'id' attribute
questions.c: The <input> must be placed strictly before the <label> tag
questions.d: The <label> 'bind' attribute must match the <input> 'id' attribute
questions.explanation: The 'for' attribute of the <label> tag must be equal to the 'id' attribute of the related element to bind them together.

questions.question: Why is the 'name' attribute essential for <input> elements within a form?
questions.b: It is required for the browser to render the input box
questions.c: Without a 'name' attribute, the input's data will NOT be sent when the form is submitted
questions.d: It provides placeholder text inside the input
questions.explanation: Form data is sent as name/value pairs. If an input lacks a 'name' attribute, its value is ignored during submission.

questions.question: What is the default behavior of a web page when a user clicks an <input type="submit">?
questions.a: The form data is sent and the browser reloads or navigates to the action URL
questions.b: The form data is sent silently in the background via AJAX
questions.c: The form clears all fields but stays on the same page
questions.d: The browser opens a confirmation popup
questions.explanation: By default, form submission triggers a full page reload or navigation to the URL specified in the action attribute.

questions.question: What does the <form> element create in an HTML document?
questions.b: A document section containing interactive input controls for collecting and submitting user data to a server
questions.explanation: The <form> element wraps interactive form controls (inputs, checkboxes, buttons) for user data submission.

questions.question: Which attribute specifies the HTTP method used when submitting form data?
questions.explanation: The 'method' attribute defines the HTTP request method (commonly 'GET' or 'POST').

questions.question: What is the default HTTP submission method if the 'method' attribute is omitted on a <form>?
questions.explanation: Forms default to HTTP GET method if the 'method' attribute is not explicitly defined.

questions.question: What is the primary difference between HTTP GET and POST methods in HTML form submission?
questions.a: GET appends data to the URL query string (visible in browser history); POST sends data in the HTTP request payload body
questions.b: GET is encrypted with SSL; POST is unencrypted
questions.c: GET is only used for image uploads
questions.explanation: GET exposes form inputs in the URL query parameters (useful for search queries), whereas POST transmits data inside the request body.

questions.question: Which 'enctype' attribute value must be specified on a <form> when uploading files via <input type="file">?
questions.explanation: enctype="multipart/form-data" is mandatory for file uploads to transmit binary files correctly.

questions.question: What is the default 'enctype' encoding type of an HTML form?
questions.explanation: 'application/x-www-form-urlencoded' is the default encoding where keys and values are encoded in URL key-value pairs.

questions.question: Which attribute on a <label> connects it to the 'id' of its corresponding input field?
questions.explanation: The 'for' attribute (e.g. <label for="username">) links the label to <input id="username"> for accessibility and click-focusing.

questions.question: What happens when a user clicks on a <label> that is properly bound to a checkbox or text input?
questions.b: The associated input automatically receives focus or toggles its checked state
questions.explanation: Clicking a bound <label> automatically transfers focus to the text field or toggles the associated checkbox/radio button.

questions.question: Can an <input> element be nested directly inside a <label> tag without using the 'for' attribute (implicit association)?
questions.a: No, the for attribute is strictly mandatory in HTML5
questions.b: Yes, wrapping the <input> inside <label> creates an implicit accessible association
questions.explanation: Nesting the input inside the label (e.g. <label>Username <input type="text"></label>) is valid implicit association.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the 'novalidate' attribute on a <form> tag?
questions.b: It bypasses native browser client-side form constraint validation (like required, pattern) when submitting
questions.d: It encrypts form values before sending
questions.explanation: 'novalidate' suppresses native browser client-side constraint validation popup messages.

questions.question: What is the 'target' attribute used for on a <form> element (e.g. target="_blank")?
questions.a: It sets the CSS animation target
questions.b: It specifies where to display the response received after submitting the form (e.g., in a new tab)
questions.d: It limits submissions to certain user roles
questions.explanation: Form 'target' specifies the browsing context (new window/tab or iframe) in which to render the server's submission response.

questions.question: What does the 'autocomplete' attribute on a <form> or <input> control?
questions.a: Whether the browser provides predictive text and autofill suggestions based on past user input or password managers
questions.b: Whether the server automatically fixes spelling mistakes
questions.c: Whether the code editor auto-completes HTML tags
questions.d: Whether the submit button auto-clicks after 5 seconds
questions.explanation: The 'autocomplete="on|off"' attribute toggles browser autofill assistance and credentials management.

questions.question: What does an <input type="reset"> button do when clicked?
questions.b: Resets all form input fields to their initial default values
questions.explanation: <input type="reset"> restores all controls in the parent form to their original initial values.

questions.question: What happens if an <input> has no 'name' attribute during standard form submission?
questions.a: It submits with an empty name string
questions.b: Its value is omitted entirely from the submitted form data payload
questions.c: The browser halts submission with an error alert
questions.d: The input field disappears from the screen
questions.explanation: Inputs without a 'name' attribute are not submitted as part of the form data dataset.

questions.question: Which element creates a visible group border with a caption around related form controls?
questions.explanation: <fieldset> groups related form controls visually and semantically.

questions.question: Which tag is used as the first child of <fieldset> to specify its caption/title?
questions.explanation: <legend> provides the official caption for a <fieldset> group.

questions.question: What is the effect of setting 'disabled' on a <fieldset> element?
questions.a: It hides the fieldset from the page
questions.b: It automatically disables all child form controls inside the fieldset simultaneously
questions.explanation: Setting disabled on <fieldset> cascades to disable all input fields and buttons contained within it.

questions.question: What is the 'form' attribute on an <input> element used for (e.g. <input form="orderForm">)?
